diagnosis.summary: status namespace is healthy: no problem pods, only Normal events (schedule/pull/start), deployment status-page 1/1 ready, pod running with 0 restarts and Ready condition true, service status-page 80->80 has 1 ready endpoint. Good to go for the demo.

findings.name: accounts-api
findings.root_cause: The wait-for-db init container loops on 'nc: bad address accounts-db' because it targets a service name that does not exist in the namespace; the database is exposed as Service accounts-database, so DNS for accounts-db never resolves and the pod stays Pending.
findings.fix: Change the init container's wait target from accounts-db to accounts-database (the actual Service name), e.g. until nc -z -w 2 accounts-database 5432, then roll the deployment.

diagnosis.summary: accounts-api has been stuck since 13:10Z with its wait-for-db init container looping on 'nc: bad address accounts-db'. The namespace only has Service accounts-database (port 5432); no accounts-db service exists, so DNS never resolves and the main container never starts. Fix: point the init container at accounts-database.

findings.name: checkout
findings.root_cause: The checkout Service selects app=checkout-v2, but the Deployment's pods are labeled app=checkout, so the selector matches 0 pods and the service has no endpoints; traffic to the service hits nothing and callers get connection refused even though the pod itself is healthy.
findings.fix: Align the labels: either change the Service selector to app=checkout (matching the existing pods) or relabel the Deployment's pod template with app=checkout-v2. Prefer updating the Service selector to app=checkout.

diagnosis.summary: Checkout pods are healthy (1/1 ready, running nginx), but the checkout Service uses selector app=checkout-v2 while the Deployment's pods carry label app=checkout. The selector therefore matches zero pods, the service has no ready endpoints, and clients calling the service get connection refused. Fix by aligning the Service selector (or the pod labels) — one of the two must change.

findings.name: reporting-api
findings.root_cause: reporting-api requests 300m CPU / 256Mi but observed usage over the window is ~0m CPU / 3Mi; the deployment is healthy (1/1 ready) so this is genuine idle waste costing ~$7.69/mo in idle requests.
findings.fix: Lower reporting-api container requests to cpu 10m / memory 16Mi (well above the 3Mi p95 observed); no limit changes needed.

diagnosis.summary: Checked analytics rightsizing. One material over-provision: reporting-api requests 300m CPU / 256Mi while using ~0m / 3Mi (deployment healthy, 1/1 ready) — recommend cutting to 10m / 16Mi (~$7.69/mo saved). Not changed: cache (idle cost only $0.25/mo, not worth touching) and ingest-worker (pinned at its 50m CPU limit 100% of samples — throttled, not idle; do not cut, it may need more CPU). Note: sample window was short (10 samples), so treat exact numbers as indicative.

findings.name: web
findings.root_cause: The readiness probe of the web Deployment does HTTP GET / on port 8081, but the nginx container listens on its default port 80; every probe gets 'connection refused', so the pod is never Ready and the Service routes no traffic to it.
findings.fix: Point the readiness probe at the port nginx actually serves (change httpGet.port from 8081 to 80), or make nginx listen on 8081 via a custom config.

diagnosis.summary: web/web-7969d6cc4c-46fdj is Running with 0 restarts but NotReady: its readiness probe hits http://<pod>:8081/ while nginx runs with the stock config listening on port 80, so probes fail with connection refused (event count 25). The container itself started cleanly per logs. Root cause is the Deployment's probe spec; fix by aligning the probe port with the container's actual listen port.

findings.name: cache
findings.root_cause: The cache Deployment sets nodeSelector disktype=nvme, but the only cluster node doctor-lab-control-plane is labeled disktype=standard, so the scheduler reports '0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' and pod cache-54f4fcc74-25gpc stays Pending forever.
findings.fix: Remove or correct the nodeSelector in the cache Deployment (change disktype: nvme to disktype: standard, or drop it), since the only node has label disktype=standard.

diagnosis.summary: The cache deployment never gets a pod running because its pod spec carries nodeSelector {disktype: nvme} while the sole cluster node doctor-lab-control-plane is labeled disktype=standard. The scheduler cannot place the pod (FailedScheduling: didn't match node affinity/selector), leaving cache-54f4fcc74-25gpc Pending and the Deployment at 0 ready replicas. Fix: change or remove the nodeSelector in the cache Deployment.

findings.name: orders-api
findings.root_cause: orders-api container exits 1 on startup with "FATAL: DATABASE_URL is not set" because the Deployment defines no env/envFrom at all, so the app never receives its database configuration and crash-loops (5 restarts, pod 0/1 ready), taking the orders page down.
findings.fix: Add DATABASE_URL to the orders-api Deployment via env or envFrom (Secret/ConfigMap) pointing at the orders database, then roll out.

diagnosis.summary: orders/orders-api is crash-looping (exit code 1, 5 restarts, BackOff). Logs show the fatal error 'DATABASE_URL is not set' and the pod spec has no env or envFrom entries, so the deployment simply lacks the database configuration. No other workloads in the namespace; no services exist there. Fix: supply DATABASE_URL (env/envFrom from a Secret/ConfigMap) in the orders-api Deployment."

findings.name: mailer
findings.root_cause: mailer crash-loops with 'nc: bad address smtp-relay' because its pod uses dnsPolicy None with a custom nameserver 10.96.0.99 that does not resolve the in-cluster service name; the smtp-relay Service and pod are healthy, so the relay is not down — mailer's DNS config is.
findings.fix: Remove the custom dnsConfig (nameserver 10.96.0.99) from the mailer Deployment or set dnsPolicy back to ClusterFirst so 'smtp-relay' resolves via the cluster DNS at 10.96.0.10.

diagnosis.summary: The smtp-relay is NOT down: its pod smtp-relay-ddbf8b688-z5tg7 is Running/Ready, listening on port 25, and the Service has a ready endpoint. The real problem is in the mailer pod: it runs with dnsPolicy None and a custom nameserver 10.96.0.99, which fails to resolve 'smtp-relay', so every nc check gets 'bad address' and the container exits 1 (BackOff). Fix the mailer Deployment's DNS configuration (drop the bogus nameserver / restore ClusterFirst).

findings.name: ledger
findings.root_cause: ledger container panics at startup with 'invalid config key "retries": expected integer, got "three"' and exits 2, so the pod is in CrashLoopBackOff (0/1 ready) — a bad configuration value for retries, not an infrastructure fault.
findings.fix: Fix the ledger configuration: set the 'retries' key to an integer (e.g. 3) instead of the string 'three', then roll the deployment.

findings.name: ledger-api
findings.root_cause: Service ledger-api selects app=ledger-gateway, but no pod in the namespace carries that label (labels present are app=ledger and app=ledger-api), so it has 0 matching pods and 0 ready endpoints and never answers.
findings.fix: Point the service selector at the actual backend pods (app=ledger-api, whose deployment is 1/1 ready) or add the missing label to the intended workload.

diagnosis.summary: Two independent faults in namespace ledger. (1) Deployment 'ledger' crash-loops: its container exits 2 on startup with panic 'invalid config key \"retries\": expected integer, got \"three\"'; fix by setting retries to an integer. (2) Service 'ledger-api' does not answer because its selector app=ledger-gateway matches no pods (the healthy 'ledger-api' deployment's pods are labeled app=ledger-api); fix the selector. The two reported symptoms have separate root causes.

Fix: switch checkout-web's trust volume to internal-ca."
